flag_rule: flag = contradicted | mismatch | framing-drift (these route to 🚨 via compose-review); unverifiable is NOT a flag (routes to ⚠️ low-confidence). Majority = >=2 of 3 reps in the flag set. The #apply item differs under analyze.py's most_common rule and is listed separately.
notes: Claims are the July ledger-50 floor; several pages changed since. Adjudication is of the claim against the page text at claim time plus product source.
4 of the O55med-only REALs were independently fixed by merged PRs citing the same claim (#20472, #21374, #20505) or human-adjudicated (#20348).
Items 2-3 are real at claim time but on a hand-maintained HITRUST page replaced by a data-generated page 2026-07-16; they would not recur today.
Item 9 (setup.py entrypoint) is still live on content/docs/iac/concepts/projects/_index.md L99 — neither Sonnet nor prod caught it.

items.claim: An `aws.ec2.Vpc` resource has a `vpcId` property that is an output.
items.evidence: aws.ec2.Vpc has no vpcId output (pulumi-aws sdk/nodejs/ec2/vpc.ts); July page L38 said `vpcId`; fixed by merged content-review pulumi/docs#20472 citing this exact claim

items.claim: The `pulumi.Config` type offers a collection of getters and setters for retrieving configuration values of various types by their key.
items.evidence: Config exposes only get*/require*/try* (sdk/nodejs/config.ts; sdk/go/pulumi/config/config.go) — no setters; fixed by merged pulumi/docs#21374 ('Dropped "and setters"')

items.claim: HITRUST CSF 11.5 framework reference '06.d Data Protection and Privacy of Covered Information' (as applied to the pubsub-encryption policy) specifies: 'Cryptographic controls shall be used in compliance with all relevant agreements, laws and regulations.'
items.evidence: Pre-#20274 hand page (b3dd76afde^, google-cloud.md) paired pubsub-encryption '06.d' with the crypto-controls spec sentence; data/policy_pack_policies/hitrust-google-cloud.json gives 06.d its own 'Covered information shall be protected…' spec. Page superseded by generated page 2026-07-16 — defect no longer live

items.claim: The subnetwork-flow-logs policy requires GCP subnetworks to have flowLogsConfig enabled.
items.evidence: Pre-#20274 page said 'Require subnetworks to have flowLogsConfig enabled'; gcp.compute.Subnetwork has only `logConfig` (pulumi-gcp sdk/nodejs/compute/subnetwork.ts:456) and the data file's remediation uses logConfig. Superseded page — no longer live

items.claim: A Pulumi project is a program in a chosen language that defines a collection of related cloud resources.
items.evidence: 'A project is a program in your chosen language…' is a deliberate tutorial simplification repeated in aws/azure/gcp/kubernetes create-project.md and kept through a human-merged glow-up (#21816); pedantic framing-drift vs /docs/iac/concepts/projects definition, not misleading

items.claim: The `.getOutput("...")` method is a valid Pulumi API for retrieving named outputs from a `StackReference` or Terraform state reference object.
items.evidence: #20348 human-adjudicated anchor: pulumi-terraform state is invoke functions (getS3Reference etc., sdk/nodejs/state/index.ts) returning an outputs map — no S3Reference class with .getOutput()

items.claim: The Go example program imports `github.com/pulumi/pulumi-kubernetes/sdk/v4/go/kubernetes` and `github.com/pulumi/pulumi/sdk/v3/go/pulumi`, creates a Deployment named "app-dep" with one replica running a container named "nginx" using the "nginx" image, and exports the deployment's metadata name.
items.evidence: Page's Go block imports kubernetes/apps/v1, core/v1, meta/v1 subpackages (create-project.md ~L303-305) — code is correct; S flagged the extractor's paraphrase of the imports, not a page defect

items.claim: The Configuration documentation is located at /docs/concepts/config/.
items.evidence: July projects page L230 did link /docs/concepts/config/; that path is an alias of content/docs/iac/concepts/config.md (aliases L16) and returns 301 live — link works; S compared against the since-edited current text

items.claim: In every Pulumi language, an unhandled error raised inside an `apply` callback is reported as a deployment failure, causing `pulumi up` to abort the update and print the error in its diagnostics.
items.evidence: apply.md L634 (July) / L631 (now) qualifies the 'every language' sentence in the same paragraph: '(with one Go-specific exception described below)', and L688 describes it. The extractor dropped the qualifier; the page is not misleading (wording nit at most)

items.claim: For Python Pulumi programs, the presence of a `__main__.py` or `setup.py` file defines the entrypoint.
items.evidence: Python executor (sdk/python/cmd/pulumi-language-python-exec) does runpy.run_path(program) and errors 'unable to find main python program `__main__.py`'; no setup.py entrypoint handling in pulumi/pulumi (code search: only codegen/policypack). STILL LIVE: projects/_index.md L99 at 4d85a74fb0

items.claim: Error handling in Go's `apply` may also be achieved using an `error` channel.
items.evidence: July apply.md L250 said 'Error handling may also be achieved using an `error` `chan`'; Go SDK appliers take func(T)(U,error) / ApplyTWithContext only; removed by merged content-review pulumi/docs#20505 citing this claim
